cim_eredeti: AI regulation top of mind for Florida lawmakers
szoveg_eredeti:
TALLAHASSEE, Fla. (WCTV/Gray Florida Capital Bureau) - Florida’s top lawmakers are planning to regulate artificial intelligence.

Amidst a host of software outages, Florida’s legislative leadership said it’s time for AI regulation.

“I’m not going to frame it as a bill of rights,” Republican Florida House Speaker Sam Garrison said. “I’m just going to say there’s legislative work we need to do to tackle this issue and make sure that the people’s elected representatives are doing our job of protecting our public.”

Details on what a new law could look like are sparse, but one University of South Florida Professor said the state or Congress could put restrictions on AI use by minors, or even require AI companies to have a physical “kill switch.”

“But, of course, it’s technically complex. How do you make sure that it actually happens? Is it part of the software, the hardware, the infrastructure? But it’s something that’s being considered,” Karni Chagal-Feferkorn, Assistant Professor of Instruction at USF’s Bellini College of AI, Cybersecurity and Computing said.

Florida is no stranger to AI dangers. The attorney general is investigating OpenAI because ChatGPT conversed with the suspect in the years and even minutes before the FSU shooting last year.

It was a human-like conversation, but not human-like responses.

“AI is not a person and doesn’t have common sense or moral discretion, so it’s very difficult to teach it what’s right and wrong,” Chagal-Feferkorn said. “And we’re seeing the consequences.”
